grants-<keyword>.notes: OPEN TENSION T1 (addendum-3 sec.7, addendum-2 sec.5): this facet scheme's keyword-identity leaves (e.g. grants-deathtouch-board) collide with the b1-Q1 ruling that pure keyword-grant axes are engine-redundant and were killed. The grammar defines the NAMES; whether these leaves are ever populated/scored is an open engine question reserved for schema pass. This walk does NOT resolve T1 -- it only records the facet scheme as ratified vocabulary, per addendum-3's explicit instruction not to silently resolve it. Q8.4 carve-out (walk-ratification 2026-07-31): the b1-Q1 exemption ('grants-unblockable exempt -- not a keyword') is extended explicitly to all three unblockable-grant axes (rule:activated-grants-self-unblockable, rule:grants-unblockable, rule:grants-unblockable-target) -- 'unblockable' is their sanctioned pseudo-keyword facet value. Minimal-churn: no facet leaves authored, no renames; their DEFINITIONS were rewritten to state facet readings (duration/scope/delivery read from member quotes) instead. T1 stays parked -- this carve-out covers 'unblockable' only, no real-keyword facet leaves get authored.

<delivery>-unblockable-<scope>.notes: PROPOSED, NOT RATIFIED. The walk found 4 live axes covering this space under inconsistent names (none lattice-conformant) with corpus hit-count patterns that overlap substantially (see ratification doc sec.2.4 -- grants-unblockable 407 hits, innate-unblockable 373 hits, measured against the SAME 'can't be blocked' phrase family). Before adopting this grammar, Captain must rule whether the 4 existing axes collapse onto these 4 lattice cells 1:1 or whether real semantic differences (e.g. duration, 'as though it had menace' variants) require additional facets. Do not auto-migrate members. SUPERSEDED 2026-07-31: see rejected_reason. The 4 axes named in instantiated_members_current_names do NOT collapse onto this lattice; see the grants-<keyword> entry's 'unblockable' pseudo-keyword carve-out and the new cant-be-blocked-<restriction> family instead.
<delivery>-unblockable-<scope>.rejected_reason: The delivery slot conflated DELIVERY with SCOPE (CODEBOOK-NAMING-GRAMMAR.md sec.1/sec.6 violation): 'targeted' is a SCOPE concept (sec.6 -- present only when the word 'target' appears per CR 601.2c), not a DELIVERY value (sec.2 -- ability structure: static/activated/etb/etc). Superseded by the terminology-law redesign (Q8.2-Q8.4) and the new cant-be-blocked-<restriction> family (Q8.5) below. Record kept per G4/G5 -- not deleted.

cant-be-blocked-<restriction>.cr_anchor: 113.12 (a stated quality -- 'can't be blocked' -- is neither a granted ability nor a set characteristic; corrected 2026-07-31 follow-on, the original walk-session draft cited 509.1h, which is actually about blocked/unblocked status PERSISTING through combat, not the can't-be-blocked quality itself); 702.111a (Menace, contrast case -- keyword evasion owns its own layer, gets no rule: axis per Q8.6)
cant-be-blocked-<restriction>.terminology_law: 'unblockable' is reserved for the ABSOLUTE form -- "can't be blocked" with no restriction rider. Any continuation with "except by", "by creatures with", "unless", or "as long as" makes it a BLOCKING RESTRICTION (this family), regardless of delivery. Duration is NOT a restriction: "can't be blocked this turn" is absolute unblockable with eot duration; "can't be blocked as long as defending player controls an Island" is a restriction (this family).

facets.note: CLOSED, extensible only by Captain ratification (Q8.5). Non-keyword oracle text only -- keyword evasion (menace, skulk, fear, intimidate, shadow, horsemanship, landwalk, flying) gets NO rule: axes (Q8.6, b1 bare-keyword kills). Extended 2026-07-31 (B1 ruling, post-execution follow-on): 'by-controller' added -- "can't be blocked by creatures [a specific player] controls" is a distinct shape from by-color/by-power (not about the blocker's characteristics) and from except-by-count (not a numeric threshold) -- it names WHO may not block, not WHAT they're like.

cant-be-blocked-<restriction>.notes: Seeded by the pre-existing rule:cant-be-blocked-by-color (unchanged by this ruling). Ratifies the compound stem token 'cant-be-blocked' into the naming-grammar vocabulary (CODEBOOK-NAMING-GRAMMAR.md sec.14) -- 'blocked' has no counter-law ambiguity, the 'countered' ban (sec.10.2) is unaffected. FLAG for Captain (found during the Q8.4 quote-check migration, not auto-resolved): The Black Gate (rule:grants-unblockable-target member) reads "Target creature can't be blocked by creatures that player controls this turn" -- a genuine restriction rider per the terminology law above, so it does NOT belong in grants-unblockable-target's absolute scope, but it also does not fit any of the 4 closed restriction-vocab values here (not by-color, not by-power, not a numeric except-by-count, not an as-long-as-<state> condition -- it is a by-PLAYER restriction, a shape this ruling did not enumerate). Per G3 (no facet-leaf authoring without Captain ratification), this member was left in place on rule:grants-unblockable-target with an inline flag in that axis's rewritten definition rather than silently moved or force-fit into an existing restriction value -- genuine halt-loudly case, needs a Captain ruling on whether 'by-player' extends this closed vocab. RESOLVED 2026-07-31 (B1 ruling): 'by-controller' added to the closed vocab specifically for this shape; The Black Gate moved to the new rule:cant-be-blocked-by-controller (quote-verified). Corpus-verified 2 total by-controller-shaped hits (Black Gate + Rikku, Resourceful Guardian, "can't be blocked by creatures your opponents control") -- Rikku was NOT added as a member (B1 only ordered Black Gate's move; Rikku is flagged as an additional corpus candidate for a future SUP/DET pass, not silently added).
